 Applicable standards: ASME BPVC Section V, Article 23 · ASTM E797/E797M · API 653, Section 6
 (in-service inspection) · Merrowfield Written Practice MIS-WP-01 Rev 4 (ASNT SNT-TC-1A basis).


 1. Scope
 This procedure governs the manual pulse-echo ultrasonic thickness measurement of ferritic and low-alloy
 steel components performed by Merrowfield Inspection Services, LLC on aboveground atmospheric and
 low-pressure storage tanks, associated piping and structural attachments. It covers:
     • Shell plate thickness surveys on field-erected and shop-fabricated tanks, courses 1 through the
     topmost course.
     • Bottom plate thickness where accessible from the shell side.
     • Nozzle neck, reinforcing pad and manway barrel thicknesses.
     • Attached piping in the range 4 in NPS and above.

 Thickness range: 0.100 in to 3.000 in on carbon and low-alloy steels of density 7.7–7.9 g/cm³ using
 contact longitudinal-wave technique. Readings outside this range require an engineering variation issued
 by the Technical Manager against this procedure.
 Materials: Carbon steel (ASTM A283, A285, A36, A516) and low-alloy steels (ASTM A387) in the as-rolled
 or normalized condition. Austenitic stainless, clad and dissimilar-metal composites are outside the scope
 of Rev 3 and are addressed under MIS-UT-004.
 Not covered: Flaw sizing, weld examination, phased-array or automated corrosion mapping. Those
 techniques are governed by separate Merrowfield procedures.


 2. Personnel qualification
 Personnel performing and interpreting ultrasonic thickness measurements under this procedure shall be
 qualified and certified in accordance with the Merrowfield Written Practice MIS-WP-01 Rev 4, which
 follows the recommended guidelines of ASNT SNT-TC-1A (2020 edition).

  Function                                    Minimum qualification
  Data acquisition (readings)                 ASNT Level II in Ultrasonic Testing (UT), current, with documented
                                              site-specific familiarization.
  Data interpretation, grid layout,           ASNT Level II in UT, current, with a minimum of 400 hours of
  reporting                                   thickness-survey experience on aboveground storage tanks.




MIS-UT-003 Rev 3 | 05/12/2024                                                                                  Page 1
   Function                                Minimum qualification
  Procedure variation, engineering        ASNT Level III in UT, current.

 reading distance; distinguishing shades of grey on the instrument display). Certificates of qualification and
 the current vision record for each assigned technician are held in the Merrowfield personnel file and are
 available on request.
 Trainees may operate the instrument only under the direct supervision of a qualified Level II.

  Block                                                     Purpose

  0.500 in

  1.000 in

 Blocks are certified annually by the Merrowfield calibration laboratory against master reference blocks
 traceable to NIST. Certificates carry a serial number that shall be recorded in the field notebook and on the
 report cover sheet.


 4. Calibration and standardization
 Instrument standardization is performed on-site immediately before survey and repeated at the following
 triggers:
     • Start of every shift, before the first reading is recorded.
     • End of every shift, before instrument shutdown, as a data-validity confirmation.
     • On any change of transducer.
     • On any change of couplant type.
     • On any change of instrument operator.
     • After any dropped or impacted instrument.
     • At intervals not exceeding four hours during continuous survey work.

 The two-point standardization is carried out on the appropriate step-wedge block at values that bracket the
 expected component thickness. The instrument is judged acceptable when the displayed thickness on
 each verification step agrees with the certified block value within ±0.002 in (±0.05 mm) or ±1 % of the
 block value, whichever is greater.
 If the check falls outside tolerance, the survey is suspended, the instrument is re-standardized, and all
 readings recorded since the last successful check are re-taken. The event is entered in the field log with
 time, block serial number and corrective action.
 Zero and velocity: Velocity is set to 0.2330 in/µs (5920 m/s) for carbon and low-alloy steel unless the
 certified block indicates otherwise; the block-derived velocity is then used. Zero is set on the transducer
 face on couplant to eliminate delay-line effects prior to standardization.


 5. Elevation Datum and Grid Convention
 5.1 Elevation datum. Elevations on all tank shell, nozzle and attached-piping readings acquired under
 this procedure are referenced to the top of the foundation ringwall. The datum is set at the intersection
 of the finished top surface of the concrete ringwall and the outside face of the tank shell, on the north side
 of the tank, and is transferred around the circumference by rotating tape or laser level. The datum is a
 property of this procedure; it is fixed by the Merrowfield technician at the time of survey and recorded on
 the survey cover sheet as “Datum: top of foundation ringwall (per Merrowfield UT Procedure Rev 3,
 Section 5).”
 5.2 Grid convention. Readings are recorded on a fixed grid of the form [course]-[quadrant]-[elevation].
 The three elements are:
     • Course — numbered from 1 at the bottom course upward (C1, C2, C3, …).
     • Quadrant — the four cardinal quadrants N, E, S, W measured clockwise from magnetic north, with
     each quadrant covering 90° of the circumference. Where a tank has a fixed cardinal reference painted
     on the shell (e.g. manway centerline), the reference is stated on the cover sheet.



MIS-UT-003 Rev 3 | 05/12/2024                                                                                  Page 3
      • Elevation — the vertical distance in inches above the datum defined in §5.1, e.g. C1-N-24in
     denotes course 1, north quadrant, 24 in above the top of the foundation ringwall.
 5.3 Number of readings. Readings are taken at four elevations per course per quadrant on the standard
 grid: 6 in, 18 in, 36 in and 60 in above datum for course 1; for upper courses, the four elevations are
 distributed at 20 %, 40 %, 60 % and 80 % of course height above the horizontal weld to the course below.
 Additional readings are added at operator discretion where visual condition indicates localized loss.
 5.4 Merrowfield UT survey workbooks. All Merrowfield ultrasonic thickness survey
 workbooks issued under this procedure, whatever the client or campaign, express grid elevations
 in inches above the top of the foundation ringwall, per the convention of §5.1 and §5.2.
 Elevations are recorded to the nearest inch and are not restated on the workbook sheets.
 The workbook does not print the datum on each sheet; the datum is defined here and inherits by
 reference from this procedure.




 5.6 Datum verification. At the start of each survey the technician shall confirm the datum, record it in the
 field notebook, and photograph the datum reference point. The photograph is included in the deliverable.




                     6. Technique
 6.1 Surface preparation
 The measurement footprint is cleaned to bare metal by wire brush, hand tool or power tool to a condition
 sufficient to obtain a consistent first-back-wall echo. Loose scale and paint are removed. Intact coating
 within manufacturer’s stated allowance for the transducer’s echo-to-echo mode may be left in place, in
 which case Mode 2 is selected.

 6.2 Reading protocol
     • Two readings are taken at each grid location, 90° apart in transducer orientation, on the same
     footprint.
     • The readings are compared. If they agree within 0.002 in, the lower value is recorded.
     • If they differ by more than 0.002 in, a third reading is taken and the lowest of the three is recorded.
     • Readings that cannot be repeated to the above rule are re-taken after re-preparation of the surface.

 6.3 Locating anomalies
 Where a recorded reading is more than 10 % below the local mean of the surrounding grid points, the
 technician shall scan a 6 in radius around the point at 1 in centers to locate the minimum. The minimum
 reading and its position (offset from grid point in the course-quadrant-elevation frame) are entered in the
 workbook.

 6.4 Elevated temperature
 Surface temperature is measured with a contact thermocouple prior to any reading. Where surface
 temperature exceeds 150 °F, high-temperature transducers and couplant are used and a temperature
 correction factor is applied per the transducer manufacturer’s data.

     • Instrument serial number, transducer serial number and calibration block serial.
     • Technician name and ASNT certificate number.
     • Date and time of reading; ambient and surface temperature.
     • Surface condition (e.g. clean bare, light scale, coated, pitted).

 7.2 Cover sheet
 The deliverable workbook carries a cover sheet stating:
     • Client, site, tank identifier, service (as supplied by client).
     • Survey date range and campaign reference.
     • Procedure reference: “Merrowfield UT Procedure Rev 3” and issue date.
     • Datum: “Top of foundation ringwall, per Section 5 of Merrowfield UT Procedure Rev 3.”
     • Instrument, transducer and block serial numbers with calibration certificate references.
     • Personnel with ASNT certificate numbers and current expiry dates.

 Data are issued as an electronic workbook (.xlsx) with one worksheet per tank and one row per grid

2. Personnel qualification
All measurements shall be performed by an individual qualified to ASNT SNT-TC-1A (2020) Level II Ultrasonic
Testing (UT) as a minimum, holding current certification against Ashgrove Written Practice AG-WP-NDT-01.
Interpretation of readings and issue of survey deliverables shall be under the review of an individual qualified
as a UT Level III against the same written practice.




Personnel qualification records, including near-vision and color-perception acuity checks renewed annually,
are held on file at the Beaumont office and are furnished on written request.

3. Equipment and calibration

Item                        Requirement

Instrument                  Olympus 38DL PLUS or equivalent A-scan digital thickness gauge with dual-element
                            mode; resolution 0.001 in




                               AG-UT-014 Rev 2 | Ashgrove NDE Services, LLC | Page 1
 Transducer                   5 MHz dual element, 0.375 in diameter (Olympus D790 or equivalent); 2.25 MHz dual
                             for wall > 1.000 in

Couplant                     Sonotech Ultragel II or equivalent glycerine-based couplant; compatibility with
                             product certified free of chlorides and sulphides

Calibration blocks           Ashgrove step-wedge SW-CS-4 (carbon steel, 0.100–0.500 in steps of 0.050 in) and
                             SW-CS-8 (0.500–2.000 in steps of 0.100 in); ASTM E797 reference block RB-CS-1

Cable                        Coaxial, maximum 6 ft, replaced on any evidence of intermittency

Calibration shall be performed at the start of each shift, at the end of each shift, on any change of probe, on
any change of couplant type, and whenever ambient temperature has drifted more than 20 °F since the last
calibration. Calibration entries are logged on Form AG-UT-F01 and retained with the survey deliverable.
Two-point calibration is required across the range bracketing the expected wall. The instrument shall be
judged in tolerance when block readings return within ±0.003 in of the certified block value at each calibration
step. Out-of-tolerance findings void all readings taken since the previous in-tolerance calibration; affected grid
points shall be re-shot.

4. Elevation Datum and Grid Convention
4.1 Readings are taken on a fixed grid nominated on a per-tank basis in the survey Job Instruction. In the
absence of an owner-specified grid, the default is eight equally-spaced generatrix lines per course (compass
octants N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW), with readings at 6 in, 24 in, 48 in and 72 in above the datum on each
shell course of height less than 96 in, and additional stations at 96 in on any course above that height.
4.2 The elevation datum for all Ashgrove UT surveys is the bottom-of-shell weld line — that is, the outer
toe of the horizontal fillet that joins the lowest shell course to the tank bottom plate. This datum was adopted
at Rev 1 in 2019 and is retained at Rev 2 because it is a physical weld feature that can be located by
probe and steel tape at the chime without excavation, and is repeatable between crews and
between campaigns.
On Turnpike Chemicals’ field-erected tanks at Lake Charles, this datum stands 12 in (305 mm) below the top
of the foundation ringwall. The datum is established at the start of each campaign by the survey crew,
confirmed clear of coating build-up and foundation haunch detail before the first reading is taken, and
recorded on the job instruction sheet issued for that tank. The reference point is photographed for the
deliverable pack; the datum remains the physical weld feature and is not transferred from a drawing dimension.
4.3 Grid references are recorded in the form course–octant–elevation, e.g. C1-N-24in to denote a reading on
shell course 1, north generatrix, 24 inches above the bottom-of-shell weld line. Elevations are quoted in
inches above the datum.



4.4 The datum is a property of the procedure, not of the data file. Where a datum transposition is required for
owner reporting, Ashgrove issues an annotated table on request; no transposition is applied within the
workbook.


4.5 Where the bottom-of-shell weld line is obstructed (by wind-girder support brackets, insulation cladding
curb, or foundation coating), the local grid station is offset laterally along the course to the nearest clear
vertical line and the offset noted in the survey remarks column. The datum elevation is not adjusted; only the
horizontal grid coordinate moves.

5. Technique



                               AG-UT-014 Rev 2 | Ashgrove NDE Services, LLC | Page 2
 5.1 Surface preparation. Test surfaces shall be free of loose scale, paint blisters, weld spatter, and debris.
Where existing coating is thicker than 0.010 in or of unknown condition, coating is removed by hand file or
rotary flap disc to bright metal in a 1.5 in by 1.5 in square centered on the grid point. Coating removed is
recorded in the survey report to permit later touch-up by the asset owner.
5.2 Couplant. Sonotech Ultragel II (or equivalent) is applied in a continuous film between transducer face
and test surface. On vertical surfaces couplant is renewed for each reading. Product-compatibility certification
for the couplant is included in the deliverable pack.
5.3 Measurement mode and resolution. Readings are taken in dual-element mode with the transducer
barrier oriented normal to the expected corrosion grain (typically vertical on shell courses). The instrument is
set to display in inches to 0.001 in resolution. First-echo mode is used throughout; multi-echo mode is used
only for confirmation on suspect readings under 0.150 in.
5.4 Repeat readings and averaging rule. Three readings are taken within a 1 in diameter target centered on
the grid point. The minimum of the three is recorded as the reading for that grid station. Readings that vary by
more than 0.010 in between the three shots trigger a fourth confirmatory reading; where variation persists, the
target is re-examined for lamination and the finding annotated.
5.5 Temperature compensation. No temperature compensation is applied at metal temperatures between
30 °F and 150 °F, within which velocity variation in carbon steel is smaller than the instrument resolution.
Readings taken outside this range are annotated and the actual metal temperature recorded.
5.6 Areas of suspect thinning. Where a grid station returns a reading more than 20 % below its
neighboring stations, or below any owner-nominated minimum required thickness plus 0.030 in, a five-point
cluster (grid station plus four cardinal offsets at 2 in) is added and the finding annotated. Extension of scope to
a full corrosion-mapping survey is by owner instruction and is not covered by this procedure.

6. Recording and reporting
6.1 Survey data is recorded on Ashgrove Form AG-UT-F02 (thickness reading worksheet) in the field and
transposed to the electronic UT Thickness Survey Workbook (Ashgrove template WK-UT-05) at the close of
each day's work. Each electronic entry carries: grid reference (course-octant-elevation), reading in inches,
transducer probe serial number, calibration block reference, calibration timestamp, technician initials, and any
remark on surface condition.
6.2 The survey deliverable pack comprises:
  • Cover letter under Ashgrove letterhead, signed by the Technical Manager, stating the campaign dates,
    the tanks surveyed, and the procedure revision under which the work was performed.
  • The reading workbook in .xlsx form with all fields per 6.1 populated.
  • Calibration log (Form AG-UT-F01) for the campaign.
  • Certificate of personnel qualification for each technician who took readings on the campaign.
  • Photograph log of each tank showing the datum feature and any obstructions requiring lateral grid offset.
  • The current issue of this procedure.
6.3 Owners requesting workbook-only issue for internal purposes receive a cover sheet stating the
campaign dates, the tanks surveyed and the procedure revision.


6.4 Where an owner requests engineering interpretation, that work is quoted separately and issued under
Ashgrove's Engineering Assessment procedure AG-EA-002.

TURNPIKE CHEMICALS LLC — LAKE CHARLES COMPLEX

MECHANICAL INTEGRITY WRITTEN PROGRAM

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Document / Rev                      TC-MECH-PROG-0001 Rev 1
  ----------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Issue date                          03/2025

  Site                                18500 Louisiana Highway 108, Lake Charles, LA 70669

  Owner                               Steven Lee, Engineering Manager

  Review cycle                        3 years, or on material change to code, site scope or process safety scope
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Role                                Name
  ----------------------------------- -----------------------------------------------
  Originator                          Steven Lee, Engineering Manager

  Checker                             James Merchant, Mechanical Integrity Engineer

  Approver                            Sean Collins, Site Leader
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1. Purpose and scope

This program sets out how Turnpike Chemicals LLC discharges its mechanical integrity obligations for aboveground storage tanks and associated pressure equipment at the Lake Charles complex. It states the equipment covered, the standards applied to that equipment, and the internal commitments Turnpike makes over and above the regulatory minimum.

The program covers:

-   All field-erected aboveground storage tanks on site.

-   All shop-fabricated aboveground storage tanks on site, whether or not they sit inside a bund shared with field-erected assets.

-   Associated shell nozzles, roof fittings, water draw-off arrangements and bottom-course welds.

-   Bund structures and secondary containment insofar as they bear on tank integrity.

Commitments in this document are auditable in their own right. Where an internal commitment is stricter than the regulatory or code minimum, the internal commitment governs.

2. Roles and responsibilities

  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Role                                Responsibility
  ----------------------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Site Leader                         Approves the program and any deviation from it.

  Engineering Manager                 Owns the program. Approves categorization decisions and interval deviations.

  Mechanical Integrity Engineer       Maintains the tank inspection program, remaining-life calculations and category assignments. Prepares the annual inspection schedule.

  Certified Inspector                 Plans, performs and certifies inspections within the scope of their held certification. Signs inspection and fitness-for-service reports.

  NDT Technician                      Performs non-destructive examination within the method(s) for which qualified. Does not certify reports.

  Process Engineer                    Notifies Engineering of every service change that may affect the applicable inspection category.

  Mechanical Project Engineer         Delivers repairs, replacements and refurbishment scope arising from the program.

  Engineering Administrator           Maintains the certification register and the document control file, including the revision history for this program.
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

3. Records

The Mechanical Integrity Engineer holds the master record for each tank. The record shall contain, at minimum:

-   Nameplate and construction data (year built or delivered, construction code, design basis).

-   Foundation and roof configuration.

-   Current inspection category and the date it was last reviewed.

-   Inspection history, including external and internal reports, UT thickness surveys and fitness-for-service assessments.

-   Repair history and any change of service.

-   Signature and certificate details of the certifying inspector for each report.

Records shall be retained for the operating life of the asset and for a further ten years following removal from service.

Inspection reports without a valid certificate number and current expiry date in the inspector signature block are not certified evidence and shall be re-issued.

4. Inspection and testing

4.1 Inspections shall be performed to the governing in-service standard for each equipment class. For field-erected aboveground storage tanks, that standard is API 653. For all other aboveground storage tanks, the governing in-service standard shall be identified on the asset record and applied consistently through subsequent inspection cycles.

4.2 External and internal inspection intervals shall be set from the remaining life determined by the most recent thickness survey or the maximum interval permitted by the governing standard, whichever is shorter.

4.3 Inspection of diked storage

All diked storage on the Lake Charles site shall be subject to periodic integrity inspection under this program regardless of PSM scope.

Where an asset falls outside the PSM covered process, the inspection basis for that asset shall be recorded on the asset record — including the in-service standard applied, the containment class relied upon and any secondary regulatory driver (for example, SPCC integrity testing under 40 CFR 112.8(c)(6)).

Deviations from this clause are not permitted at engineering-manager level and shall be entered on the deviation log against this document.

4.4 The annual inspection schedule shall list every tank on the asset register, its current category, the last external and internal inspection dates, the next scheduled dates and any interim actions arising from category or interval changes.

4.5 Fitness-for-service assessments shall be performed under the site FFS assessment procedure TC-MECH-PROC-0007.

5. Inspection categorization

5.1 Every tank in scope of this program shall be assigned an inspection category on commissioning, on entry to the Turnpike asset register, and on any material change of service. Category assignments shall be reviewed at each external inspection.

Section 5.2 — Inspection Categorization Scheme

Category is determined by three factors taken together: the hazard of the stored product, the presence of a water phase in continuous contact with the shell, and the containment class of the location in which the tank sits. The scheme is set out below and applies to every tank in scope regardless of size, construction code or PSM scope.

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Category                Criteria                                                                                                                                                                                                                     Consequence for intervals and coverage
  ----------------------- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Category 1              Water phase in continuous contact with the shell during normal operation; or a stored product classified as high-hazard under the site product hazard register; or containment inadequate to hold the full tank inventory.   Shortest interval permitted by the governing in-service standard. UT thickness survey at every external inspection, with grid focus on any water-phase contact zone. Fitness-for-service basis to be refreshed at every category review.

  Category 2              No continuous water phase in contact with the shell; stored product moderate-hazard under the site product hazard register; product held within a bund sized for the full tank inventory.                                    Standard interval under the governing in-service standard. UT thickness survey at each external inspection.

  Category 3              Low-hazard product; no water phase in contact with the shell; full secondary containment demonstrated.                                                                                                                       Extended interval permitted where remaining life supports it, up to the maximum allowed by the governing standard.
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Category is not a static attribute of the tank. Category shall be reassessed whenever service changes. A service change includes, without limitation:

-   

-   Change of product grade or product family.

-   Change in fill rate, throughput or operating temperature that alters corrosion or fatigue exposure.

-   Change of blend composition where the change affects corrosivity, chloride content or water-phase behavior.

-   Change of routing that connects the tank to a new upstream or downstream service.

The Process Engineer shall raise notice of any such change to the Mechanical Integrity Engineer within ten working days of the change being made effective. The Mechanical Integrity Engineer shall reassess the category within a further twenty working days and, where the category increases, shall adjust the inspection schedule accordingly. A change that would extend an interval shall not be applied until the reassessment is signed by the Engineering Manager.

Category assignments for individual tanks are recorded on the asset register and on each tank's inspection record.

6. Repair and change control

6.1 Repairs to tanks in scope shall be planned, executed and recorded under the governing in-service standard. The following shall be recorded on the tank repair record for every repair, regardless of size:

-   Description of the defect and its location on the shell, bottom or roof.

-   Repair method, filler metal and any post-weld heat treatment.

-   Signature of the certified inspector who witnessed and accepted the repair.

-   Date of repair and return-to-service date.

Repairs recorded only in personal notes, work orders or handwritten fitter logs are not compliant records. Where such a repair is identified after the fact, the tank repair record shall be updated on discovery and the identifying document referenced.

6.2 Change of service and change of product shall be raised as a Management of Change (MOC) entry before implementation. Modifications carried out under a maintenance work order do not satisfy this requirement. Where an MOC gap is identified retrospectively, the change shall be entered on the MOC log at the point of discovery, with the original implementation date recorded.

6.3 Any change to the applicable construction or in-service code — whether by publication of a new edition or by change of site scope — shall be evaluated by the Mechanical Integrity Engineer. Any consequential impact of a new edition on the site program shall be documented by the Mechanical Integrity Engineer and presented to the Engineering Manager for a disposition decision within sixty days of the edition coming into effect.

6.4 All repair and change decisions that affect the inspection interval, the inspection category, or the fitness-for-service basis for a tank shall be signed by the Engineering Manager.

7. Deviations

Deviation from this program shall be raised in writing to the Engineering Manager, entered on the deviation log against this document, and — where the deviation affects a commitment made under Section 4.3 or Section 5.2 — approved by the Site Leader. Approved deviations shall carry an expiry date and shall be reviewed at each program review cycle.

8. Records and revision history

  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Rev         Date        Change                                    Originator   Checker          Approver
  ----------- ----------- ----------------------------------------- ------------ ---------------- --------------
  A           01/2025     Draft for internal review                 Steven Lee   James Merchant   —

  B           02/2025     Draft revised following internal review   Steven Lee   James Merchant   —

  1           03/2025     Issued                                    Steven Lee   James Merchant   Sean Collins
  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Controlled document. Uncontrolled if printed. Reference document number TC-MECH-PROG-0001 in any communication that relies on this program.

From: Sarah Ali <sarah.ali@turnpike-chem.com>

Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 14:38:20 -0500
Subject: Process Change — T-02-003 blend composition revision
Message-ID: <20250618-pcn-t02003-sa@turnpike-chem.com>
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset="utf-8"; format=flowed
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit
X-Mailer: Turnpike Chemicals Mail Client 4.2
X-Priority: 3 (Normal)

All,

Recording a change to T-02-003 made on 06/16/2025.

WHAT CHANGED
The derivative blend composition held in T-02-003 (Spec TC-PROD-BLD-06) has been revised to accommodate the new downstream blendstock draw. The mix ratio has been shifted as follows:

- Heavy derivative component (Stream B-14): 62% → 55% (v/v)
- Light derivative component (Stream B-22): 28% → 34% (v/v)
- Recycle cut (Stream R-07): 10% → 11% (v/v)

The revised blend is lighter overall and carries a marginally higher aromatics fraction. No new components have been introduced; only the proportion of the existing three streams has changed.

Associated operating conditions have moved accordingly:

- Blend receipt temperature: 131 °F → 118 °F (nominal), 140 °F max
- Working level operating band: 40%–75% → 45%–80%
- Recirculation pump P-2231 duty cycle: raised from 6 h/day to 9 h/day to keep the lighter blend homogeneous
- Vapor space: unchanged, remains blanketed at 15 mbar N2

Storage service classification remains derivative blend storage. No change to product family, containment or bund allocation.

WHY
The 05/2025 debottlenecking of the B-22 transfer line freed light-derivative capacity that the downstream unit can now take. Marketing requested the lighter blend to match a customer specification signed off in Q2. The lighter blend also reduces the recirculation load previously needed to hold the heavier cut in suspension over long dwell.

EFFECTIVE FROM
06/16/2025

AFFECTED DOCUMENTS
- Tank Process Data Sheet TC-PROC-DS-0203 Rev 2 — needs reissue to reflect the revised composition and the new operating band
- Blend Recipe Sheet BR-06 Rev 4 — supersedes Rev 3; issued in parallel with this note
- Tank Inspection Plan for T-02-003 (to be issued) — copy to MI for file
- Operating Procedure OP-BLD-06 Rev 5 — sections 4.2 (recipe) and 5.1 (recirculation duty) to be reissued
- Tank Service Summary — entry for T-02-003 to be updated

MOC REFERENCE
MOC-2025-019 (raised 06/09/2025 by Sarah Ali; risk-assessed and approved by the Operations MOC panel 06/13/2025). Please treat this note as the engineering record accompanying that MOC; the MOC log entry references this message.

Sarah

INTEGRITY DATA HANDOVER NOTE

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  From               Wendell R. Prosser, Site Engineering Lead, Cordell Bayou Chemical Company, LLC
  ------------------ --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  To                 Steven Lee, Engineering Manager, Turnpike Chemicals LLC

  Transfer date      10/01/2024

  Document ref       CB-LC-HAND-2024-01

  Site               18500 Louisiana Highway 108, Lake Charles, LA 70669

  Cordell Bayou HQ   1200 Louisiana Street, Suite 4600, Houston, TX 77002
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1. Purpose

This note accompanies the closing of the Lake Charles asset sale on 10/01/2024 and describes how the mechanical integrity records for the aboveground storage tank population have been maintained under Cordell Bayou. It is written for the Turnpike engineering team who will assume custody of those records at completion. The intent is to give the incoming team enough context to locate what exists, understand how it is named, and appreciate which record sets are known to be incomplete so that no gap is mistaken for a missing document that was misplaced in the handover.

Two points frame the rest of the note. First, Cordell Bayou has never operated a formal engineering document control scheme at this site. Records were kept to the legal minimum required for our operating permits and regulatory correspondence, and files were named informally by whoever authored them. There is no site-wide document numbering scheme in use, and in particular none of the inherited files carry any "TC-" prefix, since that is Turnpike's convention rather than ours. Second, the site engineering function has run lean; the two staff transferring with the site, Sarah Ali (Process Engineer) and Henry Chapman (Mechanical Fitter), between them hold much of the informal history that has not been written down. Their working knowledge should be treated as part of the handover.

2. Records transferred

The following record sets have been physically transferred to Turnpike custody on 10/01/2024. Where a set is marked "Partial", see Section 4 for the specific gap.

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Record set                                                                  Period covered                    Format                                                               Held where                                              Complete?
  --------------------------------------------------------------------------- --------------------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------------- ------------------------------------------------------- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  External inspection reports (Bunds 1 & 2)                                   2016–2023                         PDF scans and hard-copy originals                                    \\CBLC-FS01\Engineering\Tank Inspections\               Partial — see §4

  External inspection reports (Bund 3, shop-fabricated tanks)                 2016–2023                         PDF scans                                                            \\CBLC-FS01\Engineering\Tank Inspections\Small Tanks\   Partial — see §4

  Ultrasonic thickness (UT) survey workbooks                                  2016–2023                         XLSX and PDF                                                         \\CBLC-FS01\Engineering\Tank Inspections\UT Data\       Partial — see §4

  Legacy Inspection Report Index 2016–2023                                    2016–2023                         XLSX (single workbook, tank-by-tank tabs)                            \\CBLC-FS01\Engineering\Tank Inspections\_Index\        Complete as an index; several entries point to PDFs that were never received back from contractor

  Fabrication / construction records — Bunds 1 & 2                            1979–1987 (as-built)              PDF scans of nameplates, mill certs, fabricator books                \\CBLC-FS01\Engineering\Construction\Bund 1-2\          Complete for nameplates; fabricator books partial

  Fabrication / construction records — Bund 3                                 2006–2011 (as-delivered)          PDF scans of nameplates, delivery notes, manufacturer certificates   \\CBLC-FS01\Engineering\Construction\Small Tanks\       Complete as received from manufacturer

  Site Design Wind Data — Final — 2023                                        2023                              PDF report and calculation appendix                                  \\CBLC-FS01\Engineering\Design\Wind\                    Complete as issued

  Tank asset register (spreadsheet)                                           Current as of 09/2024             XLSX                                                                 \\CBLC-FS01\Engineering\_Registers\                     Complete against the population.

  MOC log (change-of-service register)                                        2010–2024                         XLSX                                                                 \\CBLC-FS01\Engineering\Process\MOC\                    Complete on its own terms.

  Process data sheets (per tank)                                              Various, last revised 2019–2023   PDF                                                                  \\CBLC-FS01\Engineering\Process\Data Sheets\            Complete but some pre-dates the current service (see §4)

  Fitter repair notes (personal notebook copies)                              2015–2024                         Handwritten copies scanned to PDF                                    \\CBLC-FS01\Engineering\Repairs\Chapman notes\          Partial — informal; see §4

  Contractor correspondence (inspection scoping, quotations, cover letters)   2016–2024                         EML and PDF                                                          \\CBLC-FS01\Engineering\Contractors\                    Contains inspection cover letters; contract terms held by Cordell Bayou legal and not transferred here
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

All of the above have been copied wholesale to the Turnpike file share under whichever destination path Turnpike engineering elects. Cordell Bayou has retained a mirror copy at head office solely for the retention period required by our own record policy; no further edits will be made to that copy after the transfer date.

3. Contractors and scopes

Cordell Bayou has used five external inspection contractors at Lake Charles over the transferred period, placed campaign by campaign rather than under a standing arrangement. The incoming team should not assume that any one contractor holds UT history for the whole population.

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Contractor                                                                                                         Scope held                                                                                               Period            Contractor procedure held on site?
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ----------------- -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Delta Coast Inspection Services (Lake Charles, LA)                                                                 External inspection and UT thickness surveys across Bunds 1 and 2; most recent campaigns 2020 and 2021   2016–2023         No — procedure held only by the contractor; each report cites it by revision but the procedure text is not in our files

  Bayou NDT Services / Southeast Tank Services, Inc. (and earlier, Vermilion Integrity Group; Cameron Coastal NDE)   External inspection across Bunds 1 to 3 and the wider population; occasional UT thickness scopes         2016–2023         No — procedures held only by the contractors
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The scopes above are as placed by Cordell Bayou; they were not a formal contract split, and campaigns were awarded individually. No inspection work has been placed at this site since 09/2024. Any contractor engaged by Turnpike after transfer will be new to the site. Reports issued over the transferred period are catalogued in the Legacy Inspection Report Index 2016–2023.

No contractor has transferred its internal UT procedure to Cordell Bayou custody. Each survey workbook cites the procedure by title and revision on its cover sheet. Each survey workbook cites the procedure by title and revision on its cover sheet. Turnpike may wish to request the current revision of each procedure direct from the contractor before the next cycle, as we have not previously done so.

Contractor invoices, contract terms, and scoping correspondence outside the technical envelope are held by Cordell Bayou's contracts and procurement functions and do not form part of the engineering handover.

4. Known gaps and cautions

The following are known limitations of the transferred records. They are listed here rather than left for the incoming team to discover so that the shape of the record set is not mistaken for the shape of the asset history.

-   Legacy Inspection Report Index 2016–2023 is complete as a list, but not every referenced report is in the file share. The index carries a column flagging which original PDFs were not returned to Cordell Bayou by the contractor after issue. In practice this affects a small number of Bund 1 UT workbook attachments from 2019 and 2020 and one Bund 3 external inspection cover letter from 2017. The index remains the authoritative catalogue of what has been done; the physical PDFs are what is patchy.

-   Bund 3 records were kept on a different basis to Bund 1 and Bund 2. The three shop-fabricated tanks (T-03-001, T-03-002 and T-03-003) were delivered complete to site by road between 2006 and 2011 by Southern Steel Tank Co., built to UL 142. The external inspection reports written for those tanks (2016-2023) are visual condition reports on a generic checklist.

-   

-   Fitter repair records are held informally. Henry Chapman has kept his repair history in personal handwritten notebooks, subsequently scanned into the fitter-notes folder. There is no formal repair record book at this site. Several minor shell and draw-off repairs across the population are captured only in Henry's notes and not on the corresponding tank inspection files. The scanned copies are complete to the best of Henry's knowledge; earlier notebooks (pre-2015) have not been located and are likely no longer in Henry's possession.

-   Process data sheets are not all current. Where a service has changed but the modification was not routed through an MOC, the process data sheet still describes the pre-change service. Sarah Ali should be consulted before relying on any process data sheet for a service description more than three years old.

-   The tank asset list transferred here is the Cordell Bayou working copy and carries this site’s own column layout and abbreviations. Turnpike engineering staff should verify individual field entries against primary source documents where precision is required before adopting it onto their own register.

-   The 2023 Site Design Wind Data study is the only wind-design report in the file share.

-   Contractor UT procedures are not on the site file share. Each contractor's survey work cites its own procedure by title and revision. The incoming team should request the applicable procedure from each contractor it engages.

-   Personnel history transferring with the site. Sarah Ali (Process Engineer) and Henry Chapman (Mechanical Fitter) transfer to Turnpike with the site. Between them they hold the informal history of service changes and repairs that is not otherwise on paper. Neither has been asked to write that history down at handover; the fastest route to it is direct conversation.

-   Files left uncatalogued. A number of items sit in the file share without being indexed anywhere. These include: a small folder of contractor cover letters from the 2018 UT campaign; two Bund 2 shell-thickness workbooks from 2017 that were superseded but not deleted; nameplate photographs taken for insurance purposes in 2021 that duplicate the fabrication records; and correspondence between site engineering and Cordell Bayou head office on the 2023 wind study. None of these has a formal reference number, and none was added to the Legacy Inspection Report Index. They have been left in place at handover rather than culled, on the view that Turnpike should decide what to keep before anything is discarded.

-   No document numbering scheme in use. No inherited file carries a "TC-" prefix or any other structured document number. Titles have been assigned by authors informally, and revisions have been kept by filename convention (e.g. "…Final", "…Rev A") rather than by a controlled register. The Legacy Inspection Report Index 2016–2023 is the closest thing to a document register that Cordell Bayou has maintained at this site, and it does not attempt to number the records it lists.

5. Contacts after transfer

The following individuals are available to answer questions on the transferred records for the periods shown. Contact details for the two transferring staff are through Turnpike's own directory from 10/01/2024. Contact for Cordell Bayou head office is via the main switchboard, +1 (713) 555-0472.

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Name                              Role                                                                            Available until                               For questions on
  --------------------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- --------------------------------------------- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Sarah Ali                         Process Engineer (transferring with the site)                                   Ongoing under Turnpike employment             Service history, process data sheets and process change notes

  Henry Chapman                     Mechanical Fitter (transferring with the site)                                  Ongoing under Turnpike employment             Shell and draw-off repair history and fitter notes

  Wendell R. Prosser                Site Engineering Lead, Cordell Bayou (outgoing)                                 12/31/2024 (via Cordell Bayou head office)    General handover queries, contractor scoping history, and location of any record not found in the transferred file share

  Delta Coast Inspection Services   External inspection and UT contractor (most recent Bund 1 / Bund 2 campaigns)   Available on request; no current engagement   Its own UT procedure and workbook conventions; Bund 1 and Bund 2 survey history to 2021

  Bayou NDT Services                External inspection contractor (2022 and 2023 campaigns)                        Available on request; no current engagement   Its own procedure and workbook conventions; 2022–2023 survey history

 Executive summary
 Turnpike Chemicals LLC engaged Ashgrove NDE Services, LLC to compare the nine critical aboveground
 storage tanks at the Lake Charles Complex against the current edition of API Std 650 — API 650, 13th Edition.
 The comparison covers three specific features: annular plate radial width, provision of shell wind girders
 (primary and intermediate), and the family of shell weld details called out for the bottom-course, shell-to-bottom
 and roof-to-shell joints.
 The six field-erected tanks in Bund 1 and Bund 2 — T-01-001, T-01-002, T-01-003, T-02-001, T-02-002 and
 T-02-003 — are non-conforming against API 650, 13th Edition on one or more of the three features. In every
 case the annular plate radial width provided at construction is below the current-edition minimum; all six of the
 tanks lack an intermediate wind girder that the 13th Edition would today call for on the shell geometry present;
 and none of the six tanks provides the current-edition weld detail at the shell-to-bottom junction.




 Bund 2 tanks (T-02-001, T-02-002, T-02-003) show the widest departure from the 13th Edition set. Their small
 diameters combined with narrow as-built annular plate widths, the absence of any intermediate wind girder, and
 cone-roof frangible-joint details that do not match the current wording put them furthest from what would today
 be built new to the same duty. On that basis this review recommends that the T-02 series be considered for
 replacement rather than for feature-by-feature modification.
 The T-01 series is non-conforming on the same three features, but the departures are smaller as a proportion of
 the current requirement and are of a kind that could in principle be addressed by shell modification and
 localized rework. A modification study is recommended for that series in preference to replacement.

 4. Recommendations
 R-01 T-02 series — consider for replacement. T-02-001, T-02-002 and T-02-003 depart from the 13th Edition
 on all three compared features and, for the two smaller diameters, on four of four applicable features once the
 roof-to-shell detail is included. The as-built annular plate width (15 in vs 24 in current requirement) is the widest
 departure of any tank in the review, and the absence of an intermediate wind girder is the same for all three.
 Feature-by-feature modification to bring these three tanks into conformance with the 13th Edition would require
 substantial disturbance of the bottom, replacement of shell rings, and addition of a girder — a scope that
 approaches that of new-build. On that basis the T-02 series should be considered for replacement in
 preference to modification.
 R-02 T-01 series — study for modification. T-01-001, T-01-002 and T-01-003 are non-conforming on the same
 three features but by smaller amounts. Their larger diameters give them a lower shell H/t ratio and reduce the
 intermediate-girder gap. A modification study is recommended to price up: adding an intermediate wind girder;

12/9   T-02-003 shell - Ashgrove UT

went out with the Ashgrove crew first thing. they had the frame
up on the north side and were working the lower courses off it,
no problem down low. top course out of reach without additional
scaffold - the frame they brought is not tall enough to get a
probe on the top ring, and the roof edge is in the way for
lowering anything from above. they got what they could off the
ladder cage for a few grid points but it was not proper access,
more of a reach.

told the crew lead I would not sign off on the top course
readings taken like that. said we would need another lift or a
second frame section brought in if they want that elevation
covered properly. he noted it in his book. flagged it to shift
supervisor as well when I came off.

condition of what I could see from the frame - shell paint
tired on the sunny side, some flash rust round the manway
bolts, nothing I would call a defect. bottom course looked
sound at the ringwall.

no work order, no permit needed for the walk-round. Ashgrove

up on the scaffold today for the tie-in support work on the north
side. had a proper look at course 1 while I was there. more scale
on it than I would want to see, coming away in flakes where I
knocked it with the back of a wrench. underneath it isn't clean
metal - pitting across a good stretch of the course, and thin
looking with it in places. the low band by the shell to bottom weld
is the worst of it.

not what I would leave on the tank if it was up to me. the course
wants replacing before another winter on it - once the weather gets
into that pitting it will only get worse and we will be chasing it.
mentioned it to shift on the way down. no work order for the
observation itself, the scaffold job was on a separate permit.

no repair carried out today - observation only.

materials: none used for the observation. scaffold work covered

PURPOSE
We took the site over on 10/01/2024 and inherited a large body of engineering records from Cordell Bayou — inspection reports, asset lists, drawings, calculation workbooks, MOC entries. The filenames on the share reflect their conventions, not ours. Until Leona has rebuilt the certification register and the asset register on Turnpike numbering, the inherited files stay exactly where they are, named exactly as they arrived.

DIRECTION
1. Do not rename inherited PDFs or XLSX files. Do not move them between folders. If a file needs to be referenced in a new Turnpike-authored document, cite it by its existing filename and let the new register carry the cross-reference when it is ready. Renaming as we go will fragment the audit trail and I would rather live with awkward filenames for a few months than lose traceability back to the handover.

2. New Turnpike-authored documents — anything originated by this team from today onward — follow the TC-<discipline>-<type>-<serial> scheme. Examples: TC-MECH-INSP-0142 for a mechanical inspection report, TC-MECH-PROG-0001 for a program document, TC-MECH-REG-0002 for a register. Leona will issue serials on request and maintain the master log. Do not self-allocate numbers.

James,

PURPOSE
Before you close out Rev B of the response plan, I want to lock the scope of the rolling inspection program we submit to GPSOA. My view is that we can properly limit it to the PSM covered process — i.e. bunds 1 and 2 — and leave bund 3 out.

BASIS
The PSM Covered Process Boundary List (TC-PROC-PSM-0003) is unambiguous that bund 3 sits below threshold quantity and is outside the PSM boundary. GPSOA's audit was framed against the PSM covered process, so a rolling program scoped to bunds 1 and 2 aligns cleanly with the boundary the regulator was working from. Six field-erected tanks in bunds 1 and 2 is the population that matters for the audit response.

DIRECTION
Please draft the rolling inspection program in the response plan on that scope. Frame it as the PSM-covered population, cite the PSM Covered Process Boundary List as the boundary reference, and describe bund 3 separately in the site inventory sections without pulling those tanks into the rolling program table itself.

RATIONALE
Cutting bund 3 out of the rolling program takes three tanks and the associated interval logic off the critical path before 08/10. Keeping the program table homogeneous makes the submission easier to read. Between the deadline pressure and the volume of work your team already has open on the bund 1 and 2 FFS work, I'd rather not carry bund 3 through the same rolling cadence unless we have to.

ACTIONS
1. Draft rolling program table on bunds 1 and 2 only — James Merchant — by 06/05/2026
2. Add a short paragraph in the plan explaining the PSM-basis scoping and cross-referencing the PSM Covered Process Boundary List — James Merchant — by 06/05/2026
3. Circulate Rev B for my mark-up before it goes to Sean — James Merchant — by 06/08/2026

If you see a reason not to run it that way, come and talk to me before you redraft. Otherwise, please proceed on that basis.

Steven

def shade(cell, hexcolor):
    tcPr = cell._tc.get_or_add_tcPr()
    shd = OxmlElement("w:shd"); shd.set(qn("w:val"),"clear"); shd.set(qn("w:color"),"auto"); shd.set(qn("w:fill"),hexcolor)

def set_cell_margins(table, top=40, bottom=40, left=70, right=70):
    tblPr = table._tbl.tblPr
    mar = OxmlElement("w:tblCellMar")
    for k,v in (("top",top),("left",left),("bottom",bottom),("right",right)):
        e = OxmlElement(f"w:{k}"); e.set(qn("w:w"),str(v)); e.set(qn("w:type"),"dxa"); mar.append(e)
    tblPr.append(mar)

def repeat_header(row):
    trPr = row._tr.get_or_add_trPr(); e = OxmlElement("w:tblHeader"); e.set(qn("w:val"),"true"); trPr.append(e)

def no_split(row):
    trPr = row._tr.get_or_add_trPr(); e = OxmlElement("w:cantSplit"); e.set(qn("w:val"),"true"); trPr.append(e)

def add_runs(par, text, size=None, bold=False, italic=False, color=None):
    """text may contain **bold** segments"""
    parts = text.split("**")
    for i,part in enumerate(parts):
        if not part: continue
        r = par.add_run(part); r.bold = bold or (i%2==1); r.italic = italic
        if size: r.font.size = Pt(size)
        if color: r.font.color.rgb = color
    return par

def P(text, size=None, bold=False, italic=False, align=None, after=None, before=None, color=None, keep=False):
    p = doc.add_paragraph(); add_runs(p, text, size, bold, italic, color)
    if align: p.alignment = align
    if after is not None: p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(after)
    if before is not None: p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(before)
    if keep: p.paragraph_format.keep_with_next = True
    return p

def B(text, level=0, size=None):
    p = doc.add_paragraph(style="List Bullet" if level==0 else "List Bullet 2"); add_runs(p, text, size)
    p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
    return p

def N(text):
    p = doc.add_paragraph(style="List Number"); add_runs(p, text); p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2); return p

def H(text, lvl=1): return doc.add_heading(text, level=lvl)

def caption(text):
    p = P(text, size=9, bold=True, after=2, before=6, color=NAVY, keep=True); return p

def note(text):
    return P(text, size=8.5, italic=True, after=6)

def T(headers, rows, widths, size=8.5, header_fill="D9E2F3", bold_first_col=False, highlight_rows=(), align_center_cols=()):
    t = doc.add_table(rows=1, cols=len(headers)); t.style = "Table Grid"; t.alignment = WD_TABLE_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
    t.autofit = False
    set_cell_margins(t)
    hdr = t.rows[0]; repeat_header(hdr); no_split(hdr)
    for i,h in enumerate(headers):
        c = hdr.cells[i]; c.text = ""; p = c.paragraphs[0]; add_runs(p, h, size, bold=True)
        p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(0); shade(c, header_fill); c.vertical_alignment = WD_CELL_VERTICAL_ALIGNMENT.CENTER
    for ri,row in enumerate(rows):
        rr = t.add_row(); no_split(rr)
        for i,val in enumerate(row):
            c = rr.cells[i]; c.text = ""
            lines = str(val).split("\n")
            for li,line in enumerate(lines):
                p = c.paragraphs[0] if li==0 else c.add_paragraph()
                add_runs(p, line, size, bold=(bold_first_col and i==0))
                p.paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(0)
                if i in align_center_cols: p.alignment = WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH.CENTER
            if ri in highlight_rows: shade(c, "FFF2CC")
    for row in t.rows:
        for i,w in enumerate(widths): row.cells[i].width = Inches(w)
    # also set grid
    doc.add_paragraph().paragraph_format.space_after = Pt(2)
    return t

def add_field(par, instr):
    r = par.add_run(); f1 = OxmlElement("w:fldChar"); f1.set(qn("w:fldCharType"),"begin"); r._r.append(f1)
    r2 = par.add_run(); it = OxmlElement("w:instrText"); it.set(qn("xml:space"),"preserve"); it.text = instr; r2._r.append(it)
    r3 = par.add_run(); f2 = OxmlElement("w:fldChar"); f2.set(qn("w:fldCharType"),"separate"); r3._r.append(f2)
    r4 = par.add_run("1")
    r5 = par.add_run(); f3 = OxmlElement("w:fldChar"); f3.set(qn("w:fldCharType"),"end"); r5._r.append(f3)
    for rr in (r,r2,r3,r4,r5): rr.font.size = Pt(8)

import openpyxl, datetime as dt, re

SRC = "/filesystem/Integrity/Surveys/"
mfw = openpyxl.load_workbook(SRC+"Merrowfield_UT_Survey_2025.xlsx", data_only=True)["T-02-003"]
agw = openpyxl.load_workbook(SRC+"Ashgrove_UT_Survey_2025.xlsx", data_only=True)["T-02-003"]

for r in agw.iter_rows(min_row=10, max_row=45, values_only=True):

# ---------------- numbers ----------------
Y = 365.25
ASAT = dt.date(2026,6,15); AGD = dt.date(2025,9,12); MFD = dt.date(2025,4,28); SVC = dt.date(1987,9,14)
TMIN = 0.215; T_GOV = 0.303
RATE = (M["C1-S-6"]["bl"] - M["C1-S-6"]["v"]) / 4.0          # in/yr
el = (ASAT-AGD).days; ely = el/Y
loss_to_asat = RATE*ely; t_asat = T_GOV - loss_to_asat; avail_asat = t_asat - TMIN
rl_asat = avail_asat/RATE; date_tmin = ASAT + dt.timedelta(days=rl_asat*Y)
chk_date = AGD + dt.timedelta(days=((T_GOV-TMIN)/RATE)*Y)
assert abs((date_tmin-chk_date).days) <= 1
f = lambda d: d.strftime("%m/%d/%Y")
print("rate", RATE, "days", el, "t_asat", t_asat, "avail", avail_asat, "RL", rl_asat, "date", f(date_tmin), "chk", f(chk_date))

# ---------------- docx helpers ----------------

sec.left_margin = sec.right_margin = Inches(0.85); sec.top_margin = Inches(0.8); sec.bottom_margin = Inches(0.75)

def runs(p, text, size=None, color=None):
    # **bold**, *italic*

        if part.startswith("**"): r = p.add_run(part[2:-2]); r.bold = True
        elif part.startswith("*"): r = p.add_run(part[1:-1]); r.italic = True
        else: r = p.add_run(part)
        if size: r.font.size = Pt(size)
        if color: r.font.color.rgb = color
    return p

def para(text, size=None, align=None, after=None, before=None, style=None, color=None, keep=False):

    if before is not None: p.paragraph_format.space_before = Pt(before)

    return p

def bullet(text, level=0, size=None):

bullet("**A (1.9 mpy, carried).** This is a 38-year average that assumes the shell started at the 0.375 in nominal. steps.message:
I've written the review as `/filesystem/T02003_THICKNESS_REVIEW.docx` (12 pages). The rate that properly applies at the governing location is **3.75 mpy**, and the shell there reaches its minimum required thickness on **03/01/2049**. The programme currently carries 1.9 mpy and 46.3 years (about end-2071), which overstates the remaining life by roughly half.

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Governing location | Course 1, south quadrant, 6 in above the bottom-of-shell weld (Ashgrove grid ref C1-S-6) |
| Reading at that location | 0.303 in (09/12/2025) |
| Readings that set the rate | 0.349 in (04/2021) to 0.334 in (04/2025), at the nearest point measured in both surveys, 12 in above the governing point |
| Rate | 0.015 in over 4.0 years = 3.75 mpy; the same 0.015 in loss in all four quadrants |
| Minimum required thickness | 0.215 in (the figure on file) |
| Wall above minimum | 0.088 in at 09/12/2025; 0.085 in as at 06/15/2026 |
| Remaining life as at 06/15/2026 | 22.7 years |
| Date minimum is reached | 03/01/2049 |

**Why the two 2025 surveys can't be compared as labelled.** Merrowfield measures heights from the top of the ringwall. Ashgrove measures from the bottom-of-shell weld, which its procedure says is 12 in lower. So the two "C1-S-6" readings are 12 in apart on the shell. The inspection report's 0.031 in "step" is the thickness change over that 12 in, not corrosion. Read as loss, it would mean 83 mpy and reaching the minimum by 10/2026. The readings themselves confirm the offset:
- At the eight points both contractors actually measured, they agree within 0.002 in.
- On the sister tanks T-02-001 and T-02-002, Ashgrove read at Merrowfield's points and matched within 0.000–0.004 in.

**Other bases considered and not adopted** (each is explained in the document):
- **1.9 mpy long-term (the FFS and workbook figure):** a 38-year average from an unverified nominal start thickness. It is half the rate now measured, and it departs from the workbook's own rule to use the earliest held thickness baseline.
- **10.5 mpy (2021 Cordell Bayou reading against Ashgrove 2025):** the same datum error.
- **2.7–5.4 mpy across the 06/2025 blend change:** only 136 days, 88 of them after the change, and within reading tolerance, so no rate can be read from it.
- **2057 date based on Merrowfield's 0.334 in:** ignores the only reading in the lowest 18 in of the shell, so it isn't conservative.

**Caveats you should know about:**
- **The 0.303 in reading is not validated.** Ashgrove's instrument failed its end-of-shift check on 09/12. Under Ashgrove's own procedure that voids every reading taken after 11:20 that day, and no re-shoot is logged. The 09/17 field sheet doesn't fix this:
  - its instrument isn't in the calibration log;
  - its technician isn't listed on the job;
  - seven of its eight readings were taken through coating, with no elevations recorded;
  - its reviewer has the same name as Merrowfield's technician;
  - it claims its readings went into the workbook, but only one of eight matches.

  I still used 0.303 in because the instrument was over-reading, so the true wall is likely thinner, not thicker.
- **The rate at the governing point itself may be higher.** Measured rates rise towards the weld, and 3.75 mpy was measured 12 in above it. Adverse combinations bring the date forward to between 2044 and 2048.
- **The 0.215 in minimum can't be reproduced from the FFS's stated basis.** My check calculation gives 0.189 in or 0.223 in depending on the original weld efficiency, and the FFS shows no working. I used 0.215 in because it is the figure on file in all three records.

**Recommended first action:** a calibrated re-survey of the lower part of course 1, in service and on one stated datum, before the 08/10/2026 deadline. This would confirm the 0.303 in reading and the 12-inch offset in the field.

The document also flags record problems for re-issue:
- The inspection report was signed on 01/14/2026, while Steve David's API 653 certificate had lapsed.
- The FFS uses a superseded wind speed (45 m/s instead of 70 m/s).
- The FFS cites mill certificates that aren't in the construction pack.

The document number is left for Engineering Administration to allocate, as the 12/09/2024 memo requires.
